newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-MARY JOE FERNANDEZ ONLY SURVIVOR IN U.S. TEAM.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MARY JOE FERNANDEZ ONLY SURVIVOR IN U.S. TEAM.

text.p: The United States open their defence of the Federation Cup against the Netherlands this weekend with just one survivor from the side who annihilated Spain 5-0 in last year's final.

Mary Joe Fernandez, who teamed up with Linda Wild to win the doubles in Atlantic City, has been selected for the opening tie along with Gigi Fernandez, who returns to the side, Chanda Rubin and Kimberly Po.
There is also a change at the top with Martina Navratilova taking over as coach from Billie-Jean King.
Navratilova was unbeaten in 20 singles matches and 17 doubles during her Federation Cup career with both Czechoslovakia and the United States.
The new U.S. coach is to make a last-minute choice on her two singles players, though Mary Joe Fernandez and Gigi Fernandez will be her doubles team.
"I am keeping the slots open for the singles. It is whoever is healthiest and playing the best tennis that will get the nod on Saturday," Navratilova said.
However, she acknowledged she was leaning towards Fernandez and Rubin -- for their experience and their weapons, despite the fact the on-form Po is ranked ahead of Rubin.

"I know if I was playing against them, I would have a more difficult time against Chanda Rubin because of the pace of her shots and Mary Joe Fernandez because of her experience as well as play-making ability.
"As a player, I'd rather play Kim Po because she is not as threatening as a Chanda Rubin. I mean, I could play a great match against Chanda and still lose."
The Netherlands, making their world group debut, are outwardly optimistic in advance of their tie in Haarlem.
"The first time in the world group and then playing America at home," said their leading player Brenda Schultz. "What more do you want?"
Dutch coach Fred Hemmes added: "We don't fear the Americans. All pressure is on their shoulders and we can play freely. We could write history if we win."

Spain, who have won the Cup four times in the past six years including victories over the United States in 1991, 1994 and 1995, will be without Conchita Martinez for their tie against Belgium in Liege.
Martinez, who formed with Arantxa Sanchez Vicario the most successful doubles combination in Cup history, has tendinitis in her right shoulder. It will be the first Cup she has missed since 1988.
Maria Luisa Serna, who turns 18 on Saturday, is the likely replacement.
Sanchez Vicario will be keen to avenge her defeat to Dominique van Roost in the third round of this year's Australian Open.
Germany host the Czech Republic in Mannheim while Japan take on France in Tokyo in the other two world group one ties.
Germany will be without world number one Steffi Graf who has a recurrent left knee injury and Anke Huber who has injured her shoulder.
"I really wanted to play on my own doorstep," said Graf. "The fact I'll be missing obviously isn't that good for the event."
France, losing semifinalists in both the past two years, will be captained by Yannick Noah, who has led the French men's team to the Davis Cup twice in the past five years.
"They asked me to come and the aim is to win," said Noah. "It won't be easy but we have a fine team."
